title: I watched Citizen Kane for the first time

commenti.body:
Honestly, I think the good experience I had finally going and watching Citizen Kane and loving it was a fairly important step in breaking my film-baby phase. I didn't trust old movies to entertain me, so I never checked. But then I eventually saw this, and loved it — really loved it.

I think it's very good that the "most famous" classic movie — if you had asked film-baby me — is a banger. Not everyone gets the Mona Lisa, and so not everyone proceeds from there into other high art appreciation... but pretty much everyone finds (at least) *something* very cool about Citizen Kane. On rewatches, you find more.

Now watch Night of the Hunter.

Well Night of the Hunter really is something special.  If you're doing Welles I'd really like to suggest the "director's restoration" of Touch of Evil.  Also, Ebert's commentary track for Citizen Kane is definitely worth watching along with the film.

I love Citizen Kane. Partly because it's good. Partly because it's groundbreaking. But also because most people have your reaction, cinephile or not. It's one of those things that even almost 100 years later, pretty much anyone who takes the leap to check it out comes away rewarded, and surprised to be so richly rewarded. It's an amazing achievement.
Timeless is an overused phrase but Citizen Kane is truly timeless. It feels fresh and contemporary 100 years later.

Absolutely.

I think my next-favorite Welles is actually The Trial, but that's probably not the best follow-up to Kane. Heh.

Night of the Hunter is actually a movie that I was intrigued by and had thought about giving a watch too. Now I'm definitely going to have to watch.

To make sure there's no confusion, you're referring to "The Night of the Hunter," directed by Charles Laughton, right?

Speaking of Ebert, I actually went to his website and read his review for Citizen Kane in his "great movies" after watching and there's definitely a lot I missed.

I imagine the commentary track would be very interesting to listen to, especially since he apparently analyzed it frame by frame. His 4 star reviews are always fun to read.
